title: A DATE or TIMESTAMP against a TIMESTAMPTZ compares as instants in the session's TimeZone
verdict: `ts = tstz` and `date = tstz` are true under UTC and false under America/New_York for the same wall clock
description: `DATE '2020-01-01' = TIMESTAMP '2020-01-01 00:00:00'` is true and `DATE < TIMESTAMP '… 00:00:00.000001'` is true: a date is its midnight. Against a TIMESTAMPTZ the wall clock is read in the session's `TimeZone`: `TIMESTAMP '2020-01-01 00:00:00' = TIMESTAMPTZ '2020-01-01 00:00:00+00'` is true under `UTC` and false under `America/New_York`, and so is the DATE against it.
reference: Time-zone-aware timestamps are refused by the model (`duckdb-time-zones`). The lift plans `ts = tstz` and `dt = tstz` with both sides cast to a naive `timestamp(6)` (2 casts) and does not refuse; whether the checker refuses the plan was not re-run here (the only local checker is from 2026-11-09). A DATE against a TIMESTAMP is written as the midnight cast (#807, 2 casts).
